source.title: Warhammer 40,000: The App 2.7.1, data build 972, released 2026-10-02

data.summary: A unit has to be placed on the battlefield before it can move or attack, usually at deployment, though other causes exist. Any time a rule calls for a unit to be set up, position its models with the unit in coherency (03.03) and unengaged (03.04) and every other requirement or restriction satisfied. If some models cannot be placed, lift the unit off and send it back to where it started (strategic reserves, inside a TRANSPORT and so on). When this happens during a move type, the unit counts as not having been chosen to move, so it can be chosen later to try once more or to remain stationary (09.04). Oversized models that cannot meet set-up restrictions: at deployment, a model whose base physically will not fit wholly in your deployment zone goes against your battlefield edge, and during the turn it was set up its unit may not make normal, advance, fall-back or charge moves or shoot ranged weapons; models such as AIRCRAFT whose wings or other parts stick out well beyond the base may overhang the zone when nothing else works, provided the base itself is wholly inside. From strategic reserves, a model whose base will not fit wholly within the required distance of the edge goes against a battlefield edge, and apart from AIRCRAFT its unit suffers the same move and ranged-attack limits during the turn it is set up; oversized models such as AIRCRAFT may overhang an edge of the battlefield when needed but must still be over 8" away from every enemy unit. A disembarking unit goes wholly within 3" of its TRANSPORT; a model too big for that (typically wider than 3" whichever way it is measured) is instead placed so its base is within 1" of the base, or the hull, of the TRANSPORT, unengaged from every enemy unit. Redeploying means removing the unit and deploying it once more under the usual rules, for example via Infiltrators when all its models have that ability.
